documentation.text:
@title  MilestoneEscrow
 @notice Trustless milestone-based escrow with verifiable software deliverables.
         ETH is only released after the client cryptographically confirms
         the artifact they received matches the hash registered by the developer.
  Economic model
  ──────────────
  • Platform fee   0.5% of every milestone payout (approval or dispute ruling)
  • Dispute stake  5%   of the milestone — posted by BOTH sides ("loser pays")
      - disputer posts it in raiseDispute()
      - the other party posts it in respondToDispute() to contest
      - if they don't respond within the window, disputer wins by default
  • Arbitrator fee 1%   of the milestone — paid out of the LOSER's slashed stake,
                        split between the arbitrators who voted for the outcome
  • Slashed stake remainder (5% − 1% = 4%) → platform
  • Winner's stake is returned in full
  Arbitrator panel (keeps arbitrators honest)
  ───────────────────────────────────────────
  • 3 arbitrators each lock a 1 ETH bond to join the panel
  • Every dispute is voted on by all 3 — 2 matching votes decide it
  • Voting against the final outcome, or not voting before the deadline,
    slashes 0.1 ETH from the arbitrator's bond (→ platform)
  • A bond below 0.5 ETH removes the arbitrator from the panel
  • No 2-vote majority by the deadline → the respondent wins
    (the disputer has to convince the panel)
 @dev BCT Final Lab Project — MilestoneChain

@param _responseWindow Seconds a respondent has to counter-stake a dispute, and
                        then the arbitrators have to vote (minutes for demos, days in production).

@dev Settles a contested dispute.
      - loser's stake is slashed: 1% of the milestone to the arbitrators who voted
        for the outcome (split equally), the rest to the platform
      - arbitrators who voted against the outcome are slashed; so are non-voters
        when the dispute ended by timeout (_timedOut)

raiseDispute(uint256,uint256,string).notice: Client or developer disputes a Submitted milestone by staking 5%.         Typical case: client's verifyDeliverable() returned a hash mismatch.         Developer may dispute if the client refuses to verify a genuine artifact.

verifyDeliverable(uint256,uint256,bytes3.notice: Client submits the hash of the file they received. If it matches the         developer's registered hash, the milestone becomes Verified.         On mismatch the client's hash is stored as evidence for a dispute.

userdoc.notice: Trustless milestone-based escrow with verifiable software deliverables.         ETH is only released after the client cryptographically confirms         the artifact they received matches the hash registered by the developer.  Economic model  ──────────────  • Platform fee   0.5% of every milestone payout (approval or dispute ruling)  • Dispute stake  5%   of the milestone — posted by BOTH sides ("loser pays")      - disputer posts it in raiseDispute()      - the other party posts it in respondToDispute() to contest      - if they don't respond within the window, disputer wins by default  • Arbitrator fee 1%   of the milestone — paid out of the LOSER's slashed stake,                        split between the arbitrators who voted for the outcome  • Slashed stake remainder (5% − 1% = 4%) → platform  • Winner's stake is returned in full  Arbitrator panel (keeps arbitrators honest)  ───────────────────────────────────────────  • 3 arbitrators each lock a 1 ETH bond to join the panel  • Every dispute is voted on by all 3 — 2 matching votes decide it  • Voting against the final outcome, or not voting before the deadline,    slashes 0.1 ETH from the arbitrator's bond (→ platform)  • A bond below 0.5 ETH removes the arbitrator from the panel  • No 2-vote majority by the deadline → the respondent wins    (the disputer has to convince the panel)
